numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Multiplying polynomials with floating-point (RR domain) coefficients whose magnitudes differ by several orders of magnitude gives incorrect results because the Karatsuba algorithm accumulates numerical errors; e.g. after (e*x).LC() the leading coefficient is -1.02749361615667e+15 instead of the exact-domain value 18786186952704 obtained via e.set_domain(QQ)*x.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Polynomial multiplication over the RR domain should use the standard (schoolbook) method so that results are numerically correct; e.g. (e*x).LC() should match the QQ-domain result 18786186952704.
trigger_conditions: polynomial coefficients are floating point in the RR domain
coefficients vary over several orders of magnitude
polynomial degree large enough that the Karatsuba branch is used (n >= 100)
oracle_clues: PR test cases added for the polynomial multiplication fix

numerical_characteristics.dtype: RR (floating point polynomial coefficients in the RR domain)
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Coefficients differing by several orders of magnitude; issue example coefficients span roughly 1e0 to 1e31 (e.g. 18786186952704.0 and 9.31746684052255e+31 in test_dup_mul_poly); polynomial degree n >= 100 so the Karatsuba branch is used
category_specific_evidence: Issue #27484: multiplying a polynomial by x in the RR domain gives LC() of -1.02749361615667e+15, while converting to QQ first gives 18786186952704, showing a wrong leading coefficient in RR.
PR #27503 states that accumulation of numerical errors in the RR domain makes the Karatsuba algorithm produce incorrect results, notably when coefficients vary over several orders of magnitude.
The fix changes dup_mul in sympy/polys/densearith.py so the standard method is used when n < 100 or not K.is_Exact, i.e. for inexact domains such as RR.
test_dup_mul_poly checks p * x == px for RR, and also checks the same product after set_domain(QQ) and set_domain(CC); the passages give no explicit tolerance and equality is asserted exactly.
reproduction_risks: The discrepancy appears only in inexact domains (RR); the same polynomial in QQ or CC is expected to be correct.
Reproduction needs floating point coefficients spanning many orders of magnitude at degree around 391 (n >= 100) to reach the Karatsuba branch.
No precision (bit width or digits) for the RR domain is stated in the passages, so precision is null.

The passages give no numeric tolerance for separating correct from incorrect results; the 1-ULP tolerance question is not addressed by the evidence, so tolerance is null. The test uses exact equality (==).
